results.title: Supreme Court, Court of Appeal to go fully digital from January 2027 – Chief Justice
results.content: The Supreme Court and the Court of Appeal will begin full electronic filing, authentication, service and related court processes from January 2, 2027, Chief Justice Paul Baffoe-Bonnie has announced. The rollout forms part of the Judiciary’s E-Justice Plus Programme, which is being introduced in phases, with the High Court expected to be brought on board from July 2, 2027. The Chief Justice made the announcement at the launch of the programme in Accra, describing it as the next phase of efforts to automate court processes and improve the administration of justice in Ghana. The Judicial Service began piloting the system on November 22, 2026, as part of efforts to automate manual processes within court registries and address challenges such as missing case dockets. results.title: Government to sustain quarterly engagements with mining industry – Deputy Lands Minister
results.content: The Ministry of Lands and Natural Resources has reaffirmed its commitment to holding quarterly engagements with the mining industry to strengthen collaboration, address concerns and build consensus on issues affecting the sector.

results.title: Parents must consult teachers before pushing gifted children to skip classes – NIM Executive Secretary
results.content: The Executive Secretary of the National Interest Movement, Susan Adu-Amankwah, has cautioned against parents unilaterally deciding that their children are gifted and pushing for them to skip classes, warning that such decisions could leave children struggling academically and socially.

results.title: Food glut: Annoh-Dompreh demands emergency government purchase of surplus produce
results.content: Minority Chief Whip Frank Annoh-Dompreh has called for emergency government intervention to buy surplus produce as farmers and market women struggle to find buyers nationwide.

results.title: Samson’s Take: Galamsey – we know the kingpins, so why pretend?
results.content: Last Saturday, I asked how many more rivers must be poisoned? How many more forests destroyed? How many more children exposed to toxic dangers? And how many more security officers ought to be attacked and killed before Ghana confronts the truth about Galamsey?

results.title: Food glut: Annoh-Dompreh demands answers on Buffer Stock purchases and expenditure
results.content: Minority Chief Whip Frank Annoh-Dompreh has demanded full disclosure of the quantities of food the National Food Buffer Stock Company (NAFCO) has purchased and how much public money has been disbursed to address Ghana’s growing food glut.

results.title: Morocco secures $2.4bn to build defence industry, targets 50,000 jobs by 2035
results.content: Morocco has secured nearly $2.4 billion (22 billion Moroccan dirhams) to develop its national defence and security industry, as the Kingdom works to strengthen industrial sovereignty and expand military equipment production capacity.

results.title: Sentuo Group boss hands Black Challenge $10,000 each after 2026 Amputee World Cup win
results.content: The cash reward comes in recognition of the team’s remarkable achievement in Mexico, where Ghana defeated Morocco 1-0 in the final to become the second African nation to win the prestigious tournament after Angola.

results.title: Livestream: Newsfile discusses BECE eligibility, power outages and early retirement directive
results.content: In today's edition of JoyNews’ flagship news analysis programme, Samson Lardy Anyenini and his guests are discussing the Education Ministry’s decision to prevent unqualified pupils from sitting the Basic Education Certificate Examination (BECE), recent power outages and the President’s directive on early retirement for workers nearing 60 years.

results.title: Morocco’s King Mohammed VI hands Ali Seddiki strategic defence industry mandate
results.content: Morocco’s King Mohammed VI has entrusted Ali Seddiki with a strategic assignment to advance the country’s national defence and security industry.

results.title: WWC 2027Q: Black Queens begin playoff tournament against Ecuador on November 28
results.content: The Black Queens get their campaign underway on Saturday evening when they take on Ecuador in the first of their three games for the tournament, with kickoff scheduled for 19:00 GMT.

results.title: Ken Ashigbey urges mining industry to prioritise integrity, stewardship and community impact
results.content: The Convenor of the Media Coalition Against Illegal Mining (MCAM), Ing. Kenneth Ashigbey, has called for Ghana's mining industry to be judged not only by its production levels and economic contributions but also by its integrity, environmental responsibility, safety standards and impact on mining communities.

results.title: The Savannah Fruits Company, GIZ Ghana enter €1.3m PSInno partnership to strengthen women-led shea businesses in northern Ghana
results.content: The Head of Programme for the Private Sector and Innovation Promotion (PSInno) programme at GIZ Ghana, Arlett Stojanovic, says the German government has allocated funding to create jobs and increase incomes in northern Ghana through a new partnership to support shea collectors. results.title: Gov’t plans Natural Resource Revenue Management Act to strengthen accountability – Deputy Minister
results.content: The government is proposing a Natural Resource Revenue Management Act to strengthen transparency, accountability and the long-term management of revenues generated from Ghana's petroleum, minerals and other extractive resources.

results.title: Deputy Minister urges Chamber of Mines to sustain role in Ghana’s development ahead of 2028 centenary
results.content: The Deputy Minister for Lands and Natural Resources, Dr Yusif Sulemana, has urged the Ghana Chamber of Mines to build on its history of service and strengthen its contribution to the country's development as it prepares to mark its centenary in 2028.

results.title: Adenta police seize 125 motorbikes in crackdown on fake number plates
results.content: The Adenta Police District Command has seized 125 motorbikes in a security operation aimed at identifying riders using unregistered machines and motorcycles fitted with suspected counterfeit number plates.

results.title: Ghana Navy plans river bases to keep galamsey operators at bay
results.content: The Ghana Navy is preparing to establish military forward operating bases along major rivers nationwide as part of efforts to prevent illegal miners from reclaiming areas cleared during anti-galamsey operations.

results.title: Fire ravages female hostel at St John Bosco’s College of Education
results.content: Several female students of St John Bosco’s College of Education in Navrongo are counting their losses after a fire swept through parts of their hostel, destroying personal belongings.

results.title: God will not take sides in an election – Nana Akomea
results.content: New Patriotic Party (NPP) Third Vice-Chairman, Nana Akomea, has challenged attempts to attribute electoral victories and defeats to spiritual intervention, insisting that election results are determined by voters rather than divine preference.

results.title: JoyNews’ Nana Boakye Dankwah Yiadom, Caleb Ziblim honoured at Ghana Mining Industry Awards
results.content: Two journalists from the Multimedia Group Limited have been recognised at the 12th Ghana Mining Industry Awards held in Accra on Friday, November 27.

results.title: Mahama targets single Africa-Caribbean market under Ghana’s AU chairmanship
results.content: President John Dramani Mahama has outlined an ambitious plan to deepen economic and diplomatic relations between Africa and the Caribbean, with the integration of the African Continental Free Trade Area (AfCFTA) and the Caribbean Community (CARICOM) into a common market among his priorities for Ghana's African Union (AU) chairmanship in 2027.

results.title: Mahama sings Peter Tosh’s ‘African’ in Barbados Parliament
results.content: President John Dramani Mahama brought a touch of reggae and Pan-African history to the Parliament of Barbados when he broke into lines from Jamaican reggae icon Peter Tosh’s 1977 song, African, during an address highlighting the ancestral ties between Ghana and the Caribbean nation.

results.title: Newmont Ahafo South Mine named Mining Company of the Year at 12th Ghana Mining Industry Awards
results.content: Newmont Ghana Gold Ltd – Ahafo South Mine has been named Mining Company of the Year at the 12th Ghana Mining Industry Awards held in Accra on Friday, November 27.

results.title: Mining Act review to boost local participation and community benefits – Deputy Minister
results.content: The government’s proposed review of the Minerals and Mining Act, 2006 (Act 703), is aimed at modernising Ghana’s mining regulatory framework, strengthening governance and ensuring greater benefits for local communities and the national economy, Deputy Minister for Lands and Natural Resources, Dr Yusif Sulemana, has said.

results.title: Lands Ministry, Newmont set up working group to strengthen mining partnership
results.content: The Minister for Lands and Natural Resources, Hon. Emmanuel Armah-Kofi Buah has inaugurated a six-month Joint Ghana–Newmont Working Group to address concerns relating to the fiscal, regulatory and operational environment affecting the mining company's investments in the country.

results.title: Government targets 2027 completion of Azumah Nelson Sports Complex
results.content: Construction work on the Azumah Nelson Sports Complex has resumed, with the government setting 2027 as the target for completing the long-delayed facility.

results.title: Ken Ashigbey calls for mining industry excellence to become national standard
results.content: The Convenor of the Media Coalition Against Illegal Mining (MCAM), Ing. Kenneth Ashigbey, has called for excellence, professionalism, discipline and commitment to safety in Ghana's mining industry to become standards embraced across the country's economy.

results.title: Ken Ashigbey urges mining industry to translate economic contributions into lasting development
results.content: The Convenor of the Media Coalition Against Illegal Mining (MCAM), Ing. Kenneth Ashigbey, has called on Ghana's mining industry to ensure its substantial economic contributions translate into sustainable opportunities, improved livelihoods and lasting development for mining communities.

results.title: Toxic dumping ground: Greenpeace finds UK retailers’ faulty returns at Agbogbloshie e-waste site
results.content: An investigation by Greenpeace Africa and Unearthed has revealed that dozens of electrical appliances returned to major UK high-street brands, including Tesco, Argos and Asda, have ended up at the Agbogbloshie e-waste dump in Accra, a site notorious for toxic pollution.

results.title: 5.4m Ghanaians still practise open defecation
results.content: An estimated 5.4 million Ghanaians still practise open defecation, while the country spends approximately $290 million annually to address poor sanitation, the Ministry of Local Government, Chieftaincy and Religious Affairs has disclosed.
